answer: A scripted farm therefore has to pad 172 submissions and hold each identity open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. Because the timing is written down against the ember challenge, the vertex audit can replay the orchard history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The honest user pays this once; a farm pays it 48 times over for the same share of the pool. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
